## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Samasūpaka* ("Not eating in the right proportions", Sekhiya 34) is a monastic training rule (*sekhiya*) preserved within the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule forms part of the code governing monastic table etiquette and dining discipline. A modern English translation of the rule and its canonical explanation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 In Pali, it corresponds to rule 34 in the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha, the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga, the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha, and both the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Parivāra. Extensive parallels exist across other early schools, surviving in Chinese and Sanskrit recensions of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Lokottaravāda traditions for both monks and nuns.

DharmaNexus registers no cross-language matches reaching its threshold score [DharmaNexus]. No passages in the retrieved secondary literature pertain to this Vinaya rule; the candidate citations refer instead to verse 34 of the *Sāṅkhyakārikā*.
